Any small adverse move in the wstETH/WETH ratio (which normally drifts up slowly, which is favorable for wstETH collateral... actually wait) — let me think. wstETH collateral, WETH debt. The position's health depends on the value of wstETH collateral vs WETH debt. wstETH/WETH ratio typically grows over time (staking yield), which increases collateral value relative to debt — favorable. A downward deviation in the wstETH price (like the capped oracle) reduces collateral value and triggers liquidations. HF 1.02 means only ~2% buffer. Repaying WETH debt and withdrawing wstETH collateral doesn't require wstETH borrow capacity. Withdrawals of collateral should still work. Actually, borrow cap = 1 means almost no new wstETH borrows. For unwinding a loop (wstETH collateral, WETH debt), you repay WETH debt and withdraw wstETH — that doesn't need wstETH borrow. Alternatively, if unwinding via swapping, you'd need... Actually to unwind a loop you can: repay debt with WETH (need WETH from somewhere — sell wstETH? but wstETH is locked as collateral; you can withdraw collateral if HF allows... with HF 1.02, withdrawing collateral would drop HF below 1). Hmm, actually with HF 1.02, the user cannot withdraw collateral without getting liquidated-ish. To reduce risk they'd need to repay WETH debt (using external funds or by selling... they can't sell collateral without withdrawing it). Actually they could swap: borrow more WETH? No wait — to deleverage a wstETH/WETH loop: repay WETH debt using WETH you obtain by... withdrawing wstETH (blocked by low HF), or swapping. Hmm, typical loop unwind: flash loan or swap collateral.    - HF 1.02 is razor thin. Even normal wstETH/WETH ratio moves: the ratio grows ~ staking yield (~0.2-0.3% annually? Actually stETH rebasing ~3-4% APR but wstETH/WETH ratio growth is the stETH yield ~3-4%/yr... wait, wstETH/WETH ratio grows at stETH staking yield rate, a few % per year). But HF 1.02 with a demonstrated 2.85% oracle deviation risk and ongoing CAPO automation rollout... staying put at HF 1.02 is dangerous if anything goes wrong again. The incident revealed a new systemic risk vector: automated CAPO updates can instantly mark collateral down ~3%. The user survived by luck.    - exit: full unwind. The incident is resolved; full exit may be overkill and costly. But corridor limits... exit seems too aggressive now that oracle is fixed and confirmed.
